name: Mauscheln
description: Mauscheln (also known as 'Maus' or 'Lurk') is a traditional German gambling and trick-taking game popular in the 19th and early 20th centuries. Similar to games in the 'Rams' family, it focuses on the choice to either 'Sneak' (Mauscheln)—committing to win at least two tricks—or 'Pass' to avoid a penalty. It is famous for its fast rounds, rapidly escalating pots, and the high-stakes risk of the 'Bête' (a penalty equal to the entire pot).

history.origins: Part of the 'Tippen' family of gambling games that spread across Central Europe in the 1700s. Its name 'Mauscheln' suggests speaking in a low, conspiratorial voice or 'sneaking'.
timeline: 1832: Officially banned in the Austro-Hungarian Empire due to its addictive nature and ruinous stakes.
1900s: Remains a popular underground 'pub game' alongside Skat.
Present: Played mostly by traditional card enthusiasts and historians.
20th Century: Replaced in most gambling circles by Poker or more standardized trick-takers.
history.cultural: Used as the prototype for the 'Sneak' maneuver in many other Central European games.
history.evolution: The game simplified earlier complex trick rules to focus entirely on the 'Sneak' or 'Pass' decision binary.

setup.players: Mauscheln is played by 3 to 5 players. A 32-card German-suited pack is standard; with more players a 52-card French pack may be used. Each player receives 4 cards (dealt 2+2); one card is turned for trump and the remainder form the talon.
setup.deck: 32 cards. Ranking: Ace (High), King, Queen/Over, Jack/Under, 10, 9, 8, 7.
setup.dealing: Dealer places a fixed stake (e.g., 4 coins) in the pot (Pinke). Each player gets 4 cards (2+2). A trump card is turned up.
setup.equipment: Cards; chips or coins for the pot (Pinke).

rules.objective: Win as many tricks as possible, provided you win at least TWO if you 'Sneak', or ONE if you simply 'Play'.
rules.gameplay: The sneaker leads to the first trick; thereafter the winner of each trick leads to the next. Players must follow suit if possible, or trump if void in the led suit; when able they must head the trick (beat the current winning card). Four tricks are played per round. Each trick won pays one quarter of the pot (Pinke); a player who joins but takes no tricks pays a bête (equal to the pot); the sneaker with only one trick pays a bête, and with zero tricks pays double bête (Mauschelbete).
keyRules: Forehand leads bidding: announce sneak (commit to win at least 2 tricks) or pass (drop out). If all pass, cards are thrown in and next player pays 4 chips to pot and deals.
Once someone sneaks, others may pass (fold) or play along (Mitgehen). If all fold, sneaker takes pot without play.
Active players may exchange up to 4 cards with the talon before play.
Sneaker leads first trick; winner of each trick leads the next. Must follow suit; if void must trump; must head the trick if able.
Each trick wins 1/4 of the Pinke. Joining but taking 0 tricks pays a bête (equal to pot). Sneaker with only 1 trick pays bête; with 0 tricks pays double bête (Mauschelbete).

strategy.basic: Don't 'Mitgehen' (Play) unless you have at least one high trump card or a strong side-suit Ace. If you win 0 tricks, you pay the entire pot to the next round, which is devastating.
strategy.intermediate: The Sneaker's Bluff: If you hold a middling hand (one King, one 10), calling 'I'll Sneak' might scare other players into passing. If they all pass, you take the pot automatically without playing a single card.
strategy.advanced: Pot Management: If the pot is currently huge (due to previous Bêtes), play extremely conservatively. The risk of paying a Bête into a 100-coin pot is not worth the 25-coin payout of a single trick unless you are guaranteed the lead.
tips: Memory: Count the trumps. Since there are only 8 trumps in total, if you have 3, the chances of someone else having enough to beat you across 4 tricks are low.
If you are the dealer, you are the last to act; use this information to decide if the pot is 'vulnerable'.

variations.name: Knocking (Klopfen)
variations.description: If dealer turns a high trump (e.g. Ace) before looking at cards, he may knock and become the sneaker; he then discards and exchanges with talon without viewing, then picks up the knocked trump.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation changes declaration and exchange flow; engine overrides not yet specified.

variations.name: Quartets
variations.description: If dealt a quartet (four of same rank), player must discard them to the bonfire, pay the Pinke, and is dealt a new hand which they may then exchange.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation adds pre-play discard and redeal; engine overrides not yet specified.

variations.name: Belli / Weli
variations.description: Belli: 7 of Diamonds or 7 Bells is permanent second-highest trump after trump Ace; may incur penalty if lost to Ace. Weli: add 33rd card (Weli) as permanent second-highest trump.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation adds special trumps; would require deck and trump overrides.
